title: Customer Churn Analysis: Verified Findings for Business Stakeholders
executive_summary: Across 749 customers, overall churn is 37.7%, with an average monthly fee of $42.11. Contract type is the strongest churn differentiator: monthly contracts churn at 48.3% versus 21.9% for annual contracts, a relative increase of 121.1%. An at-risk segment of 100 customers with 5+ support tickets and satisfaction at or below 2 churns at 71.0%. Churn differs little across plans (36.6% to 38.9%), but lifetime value scales sharply with plan tier: Premium averages $1,816.78, +292.0% versus Basic at $463.46.

key_findings.statement: The cleaned dataset contains 749 customers. The overall churn rate is 37.7% and the average monthly fee is $42.11.

Churn varies only modestly by plan: Basic 38.9%, Standard 36.7%, Premium 36.6%. Basic ranks highest, but only 2.27 percentage points above Premium, so plan tier alone does not strongly differentiate churn.

Churn by signup cohort is non-monotonic: the 2024 cohort churns highest at 39.8%, followed by 2021 (38.0%), 2023 (37.1%) and 2022 (36.7%). The newest cohort churns 3.09 percentage points above the lowest (2022), indicating no sustained improvement in retention over time.
Contract type is the dominant churn factor: monthly contracts churn at 48.3% versus 21.9% for annual contracts, an absolute gap of 26.47 percentage points and a relative increase of 121.1%.

Customers with 5+ support tickets and a satisfaction score at or below 2 form an at-risk segment of 100 customers (13.35% of the customer base) that churns at 71.0%, roughly 1.89 times the overall churn rate of 37.7%.

Typical customer tenure is 19 months (median), with a mean of 20.8 months and a standard deviation of 13.2 months, indicating a right-skewed tenure distribution. Average satisfaction is 3.42 among scored customers; 27 customers (3.6% of the base) have no satisfaction score.

Lifetime value rises steeply with plan tier: Basic averages $463.46, Standard $868.83 and Premium $1,816.78. Premium LTV is +292.0% versus Basic, about 3.92 times higher, making Premium retention especially valuable.

limitations: Satisfaction scores are missing for 27 customers; the at-risk segment and the satisfaction mean exclude them, which may introduce bias if missingness is not random.
The data is a single cross-sectional snapshot, so cohort and tenure effects are confounded and no causal claims can be made (for example, that annual contracts prevent churn).
No statistical significance testing was performed; small differences, such as the roughly two-point churn spread between plans, may reflect sampling noise.
The at-risk thresholds (5+ support tickets, satisfaction at or below 2) are analytical choices rather than validated business definitions, and segment results are sensitive to those cut-offs.
conclusion: Churn is high overall at 37.7% and is concentrated among monthly-contract customers (48.3% churn) and the 100-customer at-risk segment (71.0% churn). Priority actions: incentivise migration from monthly to annual contracts, and trigger proactive retention outreach for customers with 5+ support tickets and satisfaction at or below 2. Because Premium customers carry the highest lifetime value ($1,816.78, +292.0% versus Basic), protecting that tier should deliver the greatest revenue impact.
